angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 717,267 km at 137.06 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.2962 +/- 0.0112 mas (same row, RUWE 1.11): 137.06 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.031 +/- 0.022 solar radii from Mann et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1221 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract): 717,267 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.93 +/- 0.22 solar masses from Mann et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1221 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5592 +/- 50 K from Mann et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1221 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mann et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1221 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..217M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1221.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.380, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
